scores.evidence: Gophna and Porat p. 226, site 170 (Kh. eṣ-Ṣāliḥ, 2021 1791): a ruin on three hillocks in the Ghor, about 4 dunams, with exposed fieldstone foundations; LB II and Iron I. No pool or reservoir is named, and there is no absence statement.

Gophna and Porat p. 226, site 169 (Kh. el-Ghirūr, 2014 1798; WBADB S836): a dry-built tower 10 x 7 m of drafted-margin stones, a courtyard NW of it, buildings S and E, an enclosing wall 1.20 m thick; Byzantine. No tomb, cistern or cave is named and there is no plan, so neither criterion is met.
Same record as S845-2 (WBADB S836 = Gophna and Porat site 169, p. 226): no tomb, cistern or cave is named; no plan. The chapter has no entry for Kh. edh-Dhraʿ itself (not in either site index).

Gophna and Porat p. 229, site 190, printed as T. eṣ-Ṣimādi (19-17/60/1, 1963 1709; about 0.3 km from the S1137 point): a steep tell and, at its foot mainly to the south, a ruin of about 100 dunams with dressed-stone concentrations, columns and column bases; pottery EB to Medieval, Roman-Byzantine mainly in the ruin. No pool or reservoir is named; no absence statement.

WBADB S1116 (Tell eṣ-Ṣimadi) is Gophna and Porat site 190 (p. 229; the only Ṣimādi entry in both indexes). The entry names no tomb, sheikh's tomb or cistern, so it neither puts a tomb at a mouth nor dates the only tomb as a later shrine.
Gophna and Porat units only. S845 (site 170) and S1137 (site 190) both miss C1 (pool to the east); after the merge C1 stays UNKNOWN for both (merged C1/C2/C3s = U/M/M), so neither MATCH nor FAIL.
See unregistered_observations (Gophna and Porat pp. 198, 229, 240–241; Kallai pp. 153–157, 189–190).

unregistered_observations: Gophna and Porat site 190 is printed as T. eṣ-Ṣimādi; the name Qarawet et-Tahta does not appear in the entry or in either site index. The chain's S1137 (Qarawet et-Tahta) and S1116 (Tell eṣ-Ṣimadi) records therefore resolve to one printed entry.
Gophna and Porat has no entry for Kh. edh-Dhraʿ (S843).
Gophna and Porat p. 198: the team also surveyed in the Jordan Valley and lists four LB sites there, including 170 and 190.

Kallai Introduction pp. 153–157: about 1,000 km², more than 150 sites, sites taken from maps and earlier sources, called a quick survey that is not thorough enough. Roman I/II/III appear only in the period key (pp. 189–190) with no legend or dates, which answers the open point in the 19b record.
